stem:
Express vector \(\overrightarrow{AC}\) in terms of vectors \(\overrightarrow{AB}\) and \(\overrightarrow{CB}\) shown in the following figure.

[Figure: a triangle with vertex A at the lower left, B at the lower right and C at the top. Three directed segments are drawn - \(\overrightarrow{AC}\) from A up to C, \(\overrightarrow{CB}\) from C down to B, and \(\overrightarrow{AB}\) from A across to B.]
solution:
Using the triangle law of addition of vectors we can write
\(\overrightarrow{AC} + \overrightarrow{CB} = \overrightarrow{AB}\)
\(\therefore \overrightarrow{AC} = \overrightarrow{AB} - \overrightarrow{CB}\)
diagramNote: Fig. on printed p.19: triangle A-B-C carrying the three directed segments AC, CB and AB. The stem says 'shown in the following figure', so the sense of each arrow is given only there; it is described in the stem so the row is answerable without it.

stem:
From the following figure, determine the resultant of four forces \(\vec{A_1}, \vec{A_2}, \vec{A_3}\) and \(\vec{A_4}\).

[Figure: an open polygon O-A-B-C-D. \(\vec{A_1}\) runs from O to A along the base, \(\vec{A_2}\) from A up to B, \(\vec{A_3}\) from B to C, and \(\vec{A_4}\) from C to D. A fifth vector \(\vec{A_5}\) is drawn from O to D, closing the figure.]
solution:
Join \(\overrightarrow{OB}\) to complete \(\Delta\) OAB as shown in (a)
Now, \(\overrightarrow{OB} = \overrightarrow{OA} + \overrightarrow{AB} = \vec{A_1} + \vec{A_2}\)
Join \(\overrightarrow{OC}\) to complete triangle OBC as shown in (b).
Now, \(\overrightarrow{OC} = \overrightarrow{OB} + \overrightarrow{BC} = \vec{A_1} + \vec{A_2} + \vec{A_3}\)
From triangle OCD,
\(\overrightarrow{OD} = \vec{A_5} = \overrightarrow{OC} + \overrightarrow{CD} = \vec{A_1} + \vec{A_2} + \vec{A_3} + \vec{A_4}\)
Thus \(\overrightarrow{OD}\) is the resultant of the four vectors, \(\vec{A_1}, \vec{A_2}, \vec{A_3}\) and \(\vec{A_4}\), represented by \(\overrightarrow{OA}, \overrightarrow{AB}, \overrightarrow{BC}\) and \(\overrightarrow{CD}\), respectively.
diagramNote: Fig. on printed p.19, plus the solution's Fig. (a) and Fig. (b): open polygon O-A-B-C-D whose successive sides are A1..A4, with A5 = OD. The stem opens 'From the following figure', so the polygon's connectivity is given only there; it is described in the stem so the row is answerable without it.

stem: Water is flowing in a stream with velocity 5 km/hr in an easterly direction relative to the shore. Speed of a boat is relative to still water is 20 km/hr. If the boat enters the stream heading North, with what velocity will the boat actually travel?
solution:
The resultant velocity \(\vec{R}\) of the boat can be obtained by adding the two velocities using \(\Delta\) OAB shown in the figure. Magnitude of the resultant velocity is calculated as follows:
\(R = \sqrt{20^{2} + 5^{2}}\)
\(= \sqrt{425} = 20.61\) km / hr
The direction of the resultant velocity is
\(= \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{5}{20}\right) = \tan^{-1}(0.25)\)
\(= 14^{\circ}04'\)
\(\therefore\) The velocity of the boat is 20.61 km/hr in a direction \(14^{\circ}04'\) east of north.
_note: Printed-solution arithmetic slip, NOT answer-affecting at the stated precision: \(\tan^{-1}(0.25) = 14.0362^{\circ} = 14^{\circ}02'\), whereas the book prints \(14^{\circ}04'\) (= 14.0667 degrees). The magnitude 20.61 km/hr is correct (\(\sqrt{425} = 20.6155\)). Transcribed as printed. The stem's 'Speed of a boat is relative to still water' reproduces the book's own wording, including its stray 'is'.

stem: Find a unit vector in the direction of the vector \(3\hat{i} + 4\hat{j}\)
solution:
Let \(\vec{V} = 3\hat{i} + 4\hat{j}\)
Magnitude of \(\vec{V} = |\vec{V}| = \sqrt{3^{2} + 4^{2}} = \sqrt{25} = 5\)
\(\vec{V} = \hat{\alpha}\,|\vec{V}|\), where \(\hat{\alpha}\) is a unit vector along \(\vec{V}\).
\(\hat{\alpha} = \dfrac{\vec{V}}{|\vec{V}|} = \dfrac{3}{5}\hat{i} + \dfrac{4}{5}\hat{j}\)

stem: Given \(\vec{a} = \hat{i} + 2\hat{j}\) and \(\vec{b} = 2\hat{i} + \hat{j}\), what are the magnitudes of the two vectors? Are these two vectors equal?
solution:
\(|\vec{a}| = \sqrt{1^{2} + 2^{2}} = \sqrt{5}\)
\(|\vec{b}| = \sqrt{2^{2} + 1^{2}} = \sqrt{5}\)
The magnitudes of \(\vec{a}\) and \(\vec{b}\) are equal. However, their corresponding components are not equal i.e., \(a_x \ne b_x\) and \(a_y \ne b_y\). Hence, the two vectors are not equal.

stem: Find the scalar product of the two vectors \(\vec{v_1} = \hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + 3\hat{k}\) and \(\vec{v_2} = 3\hat{i} + 4\hat{j} - 5\hat{k}\)

The angular momentum \(\vec{L} = \vec{r} \times \vec{p}\), where \(\vec{r}\) is a position vector and \(\vec{p}\) is linear momentum of a body.
If \(\vec{r} = 4\hat{i} \times 6\hat{j} - 3\hat{k}\) and \(\vec{p} = 2\hat{i} + 4\hat{j} - 5\hat{k}\), find \(\vec{L}\)
_note: PRINTED-STEM DEFECT, transcribed verbatim. The book prints \(\vec{r} = 4\hat{i} \times 6\hat{j} - 3\hat{k}\) with a MULTIPLICATION SIGN where a plus belongs; verified on the rendered page at 7x, where the same line prints an unambiguous '+' in \(\vec{p} = 2\hat{i} + 4\hat{j} - 5\hat{k}\), so the two glyphs are distinguishable and this is not a misreading. The book's own worked solution uses the determinant row (4, 6, -3), i.e. it treats \(\vec{r} = 4\hat{i} + 6\hat{j} - 3\hat{k}\). Taking the printed stem literally, \((4\hat{i}) \times (6\hat{j}) = 24\hat{k}\), so \(\vec{r} = 21\hat{k}\) and \(\vec{r} \times \vec{p} = -84\hat{i} + 42\hat{j}\), which matches neither the book's working nor its answer - so the intended operator is '+'. Separately, the printed final line sets a VECTOR ARROW over the last k (\(\vec{k}\)) while the i and j of the same line carry hats; transcribed with hats throughout, since an arrow on a unit vector would be a second, misleading claim. Neither defect changes the answer.

stem: If \(\vec{A} = 5\hat{i} + 6\hat{j} + 4\hat{k}\) and \(\vec{B} = 2\hat{i} - 2\hat{j} + 3\hat{k}\), determine the angle between \(\vec{A}\) and \(\vec{B}\).
solution:
\(\vec{A} \cdot \vec{B} = A B \cos\theta = A_x B_x + A_y B_y + A_z B_z\)
\(\cos\theta = \dfrac{A_x B_x + A_y B_y + A_z B_z}{A B}\)
\(\cos\theta = \dfrac{A_x B_x + A_y B_y + A_z B_z}{\sqrt{A_x^{2} + A_y^{2} + A_z^{2}}\,\sqrt{B_x^{2} + B_y^{2} + B_z^{2}}}\)
\(\cos\theta = \dfrac{(5)(2) + (6)(-2) + (4)(3)}{\sqrt{25 + 36 + 16}\,\sqrt{4 + 4 + 9}}\)
\(= \dfrac{10}{\sqrt{77}\cdot\sqrt{17}} = 0.2764\)
\(\theta = \cos^{-1} 0.2765 = 73^{\circ}58'\)
_note: Printed-solution inconsistency, transcribed verbatim and NOT answer-affecting at the stated precision. The working evaluates \(\cos\theta = 0.2764\) and the very next line takes the inverse cosine of 0.2765 - the book disagreeing with itself one line apart. The exact value is \(10/\sqrt{1309} = 0.276395\), whose inverse cosine is \(73.9548^{\circ} = 73^{\circ}57'\); the book prints \(73^{\circ}58'\). (Even its own 0.2765 gives \(73^{\circ}57'\), so the printed minutes are one arcminute high on either reading.)

stem: Given \(\vec{P} = 4\hat{i} - \hat{j} + 8\hat{k}\) and \(\vec{Q} = 2\hat{i} - m\hat{j} + 4\hat{k}\), find \(m\) if \(\vec{P}\) and \(\vec{Q}\) have the same direction.
solution:
Since \(\vec{P}\) and \(\vec{Q}\) have the same direction, their corresponding components must be in the same proportion, i.e.,
\(\dfrac{P_x}{Q_x} = \dfrac{P_y}{Q_y} = \dfrac{P_z}{Q_z}\)
\(\dfrac{4}{2} = \dfrac{-1}{-m} = \dfrac{8}{4}\)
\(\therefore m = \dfrac{1}{2}\)

stem:
Find the derivatives of the functions.
(a) \(f(x) = x^{8}\)
(b) \(f(x) = x^{3} + \sin x\)
(c) \(f(x) = x^{3}\sin x\)
solution:
(a) Using \(\dfrac{dx^{n}}{dx} = nx^{n-1}\),
\(\dfrac{d(x^{8})}{dx} = 8x^{7}\)
(b) Using \(\dfrac{d}{dx}(f_1(x) + f_2(x)) = \dfrac{df_1(x)}{dx} + \dfrac{df_2(x)}{dx}\) and \(\dfrac{d(\sin x)}{dx} = \cos x\)
\(\dfrac{d}{dx}(x^{3} + \sin x) = \dfrac{d(x^{3})}{dx} + \dfrac{d(\sin x)}{dx} = 3x^{2} + \cos x\)
(c) Using \(\dfrac{d}{dx}(f_1(x)\,f_2(x)) = f_1(x)\dfrac{df_2(x)}{dx} + \dfrac{df_1(x)}{dx}f_2(x)\) and \(\dfrac{d(\sin x)}{dx} = \cos x\)
\(\dfrac{d}{dx}(x^{3}\sin x) = x^{3}\dfrac{d(\sin x)}{dx} + \dfrac{d(x^{3})}{dx}\sin x = x^{3}\cos x + 3x^{2}\sin x\)

stem:
Evaluate the following integrals:
(a) \(\displaystyle\int x^{8}\,dx\)
(b) \(\displaystyle\int_{2}^{5} x^{2}\,dx\)
(c) \(\displaystyle\int (x + \sin x)\,dx\)
solution:
(a) Using formula \(\displaystyle\int x^{n}dx = \dfrac{x^{n+1}}{n+1}\), \(\displaystyle\int x^{8}dx = \dfrac{x^{9}}{9}\)
(b) Using Eq. (2.44),
\(\displaystyle\int_{2}^{5} x^{2}dx = \left.\dfrac{x^{3}}{3}\right|_{2}^{5} = \dfrac{5^{3}}{3} - \dfrac{2^{3}}{3} = \dfrac{125 - 8}{3} = \dfrac{117}{3}\)
(c) Using Eq. (2.45),
\(\displaystyle\int (f_1(x) + f_2(x))\,dx = \int f_1(x)dx + \int f_2(x)dx\)
and \(\displaystyle\int \sin x\,dx = \cos x\), we get \(\displaystyle\int (x + \sin x)\,dx\)
\(\displaystyle\int x\,dx + \int \sin x\,dx = \dfrac{x^{2}}{2} - \cos x\)
_note: PRINTED-SOLUTION DEFECT, transcribed verbatim. Part (c) cites \(\int \sin x\,dx = \cos x\); the correct antiderivative is \(-\cos x\), and THE SAME PAGE prints Eq. (2.49) as \(\int \sin x\,dx = -\cos x\), so the book contradicts itself within one page. The final answer \(x^{2}/2 - \cos x\) is correct, so the error is confined to the cited intermediate step - but as printed it teaches the wrong antiderivative, which makes it a candidate for apply-solved-fixes.ts plus an errata bracket (NOT run in this pass). Minor, separate: part (b) leaves \(117/3\) unsimplified (= 39).
